title: Frameworks: LangGraph state, LangChain tools and LlamaIndex retrieval
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects frameworks: langgraph state, langchain tools and llamaindex retrieval with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Run equivalent task fixtures through the plain state machine and the framework graph.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Frameworks package orchestration mechanisms; they do not define your quality contract. LangGraph exposes nodes, edges, shared state, conditional routing and persisted checkpoints. LangChain's current create_agent interface combines models and tools with standardized messages. LlamaIndex provides ingestion/retrieval abstractions for data-grounded applications.

Choose based on required control. A fixed classify-and-report pipeline needs little autonomous behavior. A resumable investigation with approval may benefit from a state graph. Keep domain validation outside framework-specific callbacks.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: The local graph lab declares typed state, adds read and draft nodes, connects START to read to draft to END, and invokes the graph on a synthetic failure ID. Conditional edges route insufficient evidence to review. A checkpointer persists state using a thread identity scoped to the user and tenant.

Interrupt before side effects, display the exact proposed action, then resume only with recorded approval. Parallel independent reads may merge results; define reducer semantics to avoid lost updates. Pin framework versions and run contract tests against upgrades.
sections.code:
from typing import TypedDict
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph,START,END
class State(TypedDict):
    failure_id:str
    draft:str
def draft(s):return {'draft':'Review '+s['failure_id']}
g=StateGraph(State);g.add_node('draft',draft)
g.add_edge(START,'draft');g.add_edge('draft',END)
app=g.compile()
print(app.invoke({'failure_id':'F1','draft':''}))

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A checkpoint is mistaken for an authorization grant, so a resumed task applies an old patch after permissions changed. Parallel nodes overwrite the same evidence list because no merge policy exists.

Test restart/resume, state serialization, tenant-scoped thread IDs, duplicate execution and stale approvals. Mock the model boundary while testing graph routing; reserve live calls for the model's decisions.

paragraphs: Run equivalent task fixtures through the plain state machine and the framework graph. Compare outputs, tool traces and error behavior. Framework convenience is valuable when it reduces your orchestration burden without obscuring policy enforcement.

exercise.prompt: Implement the function in the editor. def route(state):. Use the worked contract, handle the stated boundary cases, and inspect the behavior checks.
exercise.solution:
def route(state):
    if not state.get('evidence'):return 'review'
    if state.get('write_requested') and not state.get('approved'):return 'approval'
    return 'draft'
